questions.question: Why does an auth interceptor call `req.clone()` instead of mutating `req` directly?
options: HttpRequest objects are immutable, so clone() is required to produce a modified copy
clone() is just a stylistic convention with no functional difference
Mutating req would throw a compile-time TypeScript error only
clone() is required only when running in SSR
questions.explanation: HttpRequest instances are immutable; `clone()` returns a new request with the requested changes (like an added header) applied.

questions.question: How do you register functional interceptors for an app using `provideHttpClient`?
options: By adding them to the `declarations` array of an NgModule
By injecting them manually into every component that calls HttpClient
They register themselves automatically once defined
questions.explanation: `withInterceptors` is the functional provider API for wiring one or more interceptor functions into HttpClient's pipeline.

questions.question: In what order do multiple interceptors run on the way an HTTP response comes back?
options: The same order they were registered in, for both requests and responses
Reverse of the registration order — they run outbound in array order and inbound in the opposite order
Randomly, since RxJS does not guarantee ordering
Only the first interceptor in the array ever sees the response
questions.explanation: Interceptors form a chain: requests flow through in array order, and responses flow back through the same chain in reverse, like middleware.

questions.question: Why can an interceptor function call `inject(Router)` even though it isn't a class?
options: It can't — this would throw a runtime error
Angular runs interceptor functions within an active injection context, so inject() works outside of class constructors too
Router is a global variable in Angular, not an injectable service
Only class-based HttpInterceptor implementations can use inject()
questions.explanation: Functional interceptors execute inside an Angular injection context, which is what allows `inject()` to resolve dependencies without a constructor.
